blocks.what_we_do: We compare the allele pairs from the laboratory with the supplied plus-strand annotation. We flip the pairs that are complementary. We remove the sites that are ambiguous or incompatible.
blocks.why:
An [allele](../docs/glossary.md#allele) is one of the versions of a variant, written as a base: A, C, G or T. DNA has two strands, and the bases pair up in a fixed way: A with T, and C with G. An A/C site on one strand reads T/G on the other strand.

Some sites are [palindromic](../docs/glossary.md#palindromic-snp): A/T and C/G. After a strand flip, they show the same pair as before. So the pair alone cannot tell us the orientation. This course removes these sites instead of guessing from allele frequency.

Allele order is not strand. A/G and G/A contain the same pair.
blocks.you_need: You need the BIM file from 2.1, the annotation from 1.1 and the PGEN files from 2.2.
blocks.command:
```{r s2-5}
bim <- read_ws(paste0(cfg$input, ".bim"), header = FALSE)
ann <- guided_table(file.path(cfg$data_dir, "array", "sim2026_array_annotation.tsv"))
k <- match(bim[[2]], ann$Name)
stopifnot(!anyNA(k))
pair <- function(a, b) ifelse(a < b, paste0(a, b), paste0(b, a))
observed <- pair(bim[[5]], bim[[6]])
reference <- pair(ann$Ref_Plus[k], ann$Alt_Plus[k])
complement <- chartr("ACGT", "TGCA", reference)
complement <- pair(substr(complement, 1, 1), substr(complement, 2, 2))
palindromic <- reference %in% c("AT", "CG")
flip <- !palindromic & observed != reference & observed == complement
exclude <- palindromic | (observed != reference & observed != complement)
flip_file <- guided_list(bim[[2]][flip], guided_path(cfg, "2.5", "flip.txt"))
exclude_file <- guided_list(bim[[2]][exclude], guided_path(cfg, "2.5", "exclude.txt"))
stopifnot(sum(flip) == 400L, sum(exclude) == 3013L)
run_plink(cfg, c("--pfile", guided_path(cfg, "2.2"), "--flip", flip_file, "--exclude", exclude_file,
  "--make-pgen", "--out", guided_path(cfg, "2.5")))
stopifnot(all(guided_counts(guided_path(cfg, "2.5")) == c(2016, 296510)))
ops <- data.frame(option = c("--flip", "--exclude"), value = c(flip_file, exclude_file))
guided_register(cfg, "2.5", "2.2", 2016, 296510, operations = ops)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --pfile results/guided/s2-2_state --flip results/guided/s2-5_flip.txt --exclude results/guided/s2-5_exclude.txt --make-pgen --out results/guided/s2-5_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--flip` replaces each base by its complement at the listed IDs. It does not swap the effect allele. `--exclude` removes the listed IDs; `--make-pgen` saves the corrected copy. `--out` sets the prefix of the output file names. `--threads 2` limits PLINK to two worker threads. `--memory 2048` sets the memory budget to 2048 MiB. The R helper prints the exact command with your own safe paths.
blocks.expected_result:
400 sites are flipped and 3,013 sites are excluded. 2,016 samples and 296,510 variants remain. The planted problem categories overlap, so do not simply add their nominal counts.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and the expected counts passed on Windows.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error message. Check the input file named in the message. Check that the previous step finished. Keep the command and the console output (the text printed in R). Do not use files from a different version of the dataset. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.what_this_check_can_reveal: It can reveal strand differences, palindromic sites and incompatible alleles. Agreement with this annotation does not prove that the genome reference sequence itself is correct.
blocks.quick_check:
Can A/T versus T/A tell you whether the strand is correct?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. The pair is palindromic, so the strand cannot be found from the pair alone.

</details>
blocks.files_created: The flip and exclusion lists, and `s2-5_state.pgen/.pvar/.psam`.
